Registers are devices that temporarily store and transfer data.
INTRODUCTIONM
Storage registers are designed primarily for temporary storage of data. They are constructed from flip-flop ICs.
Shift registers are designed primarily for transferring data from one circuit to another. They are packaged in individual ICs.
Let's begin the lesson on 4 BIT SHIFT REGISTER............................
LESSON MENU
A 4 bit shift register is designed to transfer or shift four bits of binary data from one circuit to another.
DISCUSSION
There are also 5, 8 and 16 (and larger) bit registers that perform the same shifting functions...
Let's look more closely at the 4 bit shift register........
Notice the register can shift serial or parallel data.
The mode control input sets the register for serial or parallel transfer.
Remember that serial data is transferred one bit at a time.
Remember that parallel data transfers all bits at one time.
Additional logic is required in a register that accepts serial or parallel data.
Let's look at how the mode control input selects between serial or parallel data.
When the mode control input is high, data at the parallel input is enabled.
The high input disables gate 1. The output is always low.s
Gate 2 is enabled by the mode control high. The output depends on the parallel data input.
The outputs from gates 1 and 2 are inputs to gate 9.
The output from gate 9 is applied to the D input of flip-flop A.
Let's parallel shift 1010 into the register................
With a Mode Control Input of 1, gates 1, 3, 5 and 7 are disabled.
A Mode Control Input of 1 enables gates 2, 4, 6 and 8.
The parallel data 1010 is shifted into the register.
The data is gated through gates 9,10, 11 and 12 and applied to the D input of flip-flops A, B, C and D.
On the positive edge of the clock pulse, the data is stored on outputs QA, QB, QC and QD.
Notice the Q outputs remain even when the inputs are removed.
Touch NEXT to observe the serial shifting of 1010 into the register.
The data 1010 was serially transferred into the register.

Remember, there is always serial or parallel data present at the register's output.
The serial data is present only at the QD output.
The parallel data is present at all four Q outputs.
A feedback path between QD and the serial input allows data to circulate.
In the circulate position, serial output data returns to the register.
Data transferred in this manner is called right shift. Touch NEXT and observe the operation.
A shift register can also SHIFT LEFT by using the parallel data inputs and outputs and adding a clock pulse.
Shift left is used in registers that perform math operations.
The content of the register is ABCD. The data will shift one place to the left.
At the first clock pulse, the data is shifted to the parallel outputs.
The data is transferred to the parallel inputs of the flip-flops.
Finally, the data enters the flip-flop. Note, the data is shifted one flip-flop to the left. Touch NEXT and observe three more clock pulses.
In each clock pulse, the data is transferred in parallel and shifts one bit to the left. Touch NEXT and observe three more clock pulses.
Placing S1 to the load position allows new data to be entered on the left or right side of the register.
